chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:

When this verse was revealed to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family): 'Whoever comes with a good deed will have a reward better than it,' the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O Allah, increase it for me.' So Allah, Exalted and Glorified is He, revealed: 'Whoever comes with a good deed will have ten times the like of it.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O Allah, increase it for me.' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed to him: 'Who is it that will loan Allah a goodly loan so He may multiply it for him many times over?' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) learned that the abundance from Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, is uncountable and has no end.

key_terms.عَشْرُ أَمْثَالِهَا: Ten times the like of it
key_terms.قَرْضٌ حَسَنٌ: Goodly loan (metaphor for giving in Allah's path)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Prophet's request 'O Allah, increase it' in relation to Quranic verses?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* highlights the theological concept of *tadarru'* (humble supplication) as a means to elevate spiritual status, linking the Prophet’s request to the progressive revelation of verses in Surah Al-An'am and Surah Muhammad. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that divine reward is not merely quantitative but qualitatively boundless, reflecting the infinite generosity (*Karam*) of Allah. The text serves as a foundational proof for the principle that good deeds are multiplied beyond human calculation, encouraging continuous spiritual striving.
